page: Microsoft Azure F80alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 80 physical cores and 80 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration running at 4.5 GHz. CPU allocation is dedicated, supported by cache levels of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3. The system includes 160.0 GB of memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per-core ratio characteristic of compute-focused platforms. Local storage is bundled as a 9,448 GB NVMe SSD array, while dedicated GPU accelerators are omitted.

Benchmark results place the processor in the top tier across multi-core execution metrics, achieving 290,383.74 in stress-ng and 128,198.66 in PassMark CPU tests. The architecture supports vector extensions including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic acceleration such as AES and SHA-NI. The memory subsystem demonstrates 477.11 GB/sec large-block uncached read bandwidth and 213.08 GB/sec write bandwidth. High throughput is reflected in application benchmarks, yielding 204.83 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 114.32 GB/sec in static web serving. While small-to-medium model LLM prompt processing achieves top-tier token throughput, token generation on large 70B models operates at lower throughput without discrete accelerators.

The 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio represents a functional tradeoff, trading deep memory capacity for dense processing throughput. Workloads requiring excessive RAM per thread are better suited for memory-optimized tiers. Nonetheless, the high core count combined with nearly 9.5 TB of fast local NVMe storage delivers high operational efficiency for CPU-bound tasks needing rapid temporary storage. The instance fits high-concurrency web serving, batch data compression and decompression pipelines, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and distributed database or caching workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F80alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 80 dedicated physical cores (80 vCPUs) clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the instance provides 160 GB of RAM alongside 9,448 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage without dedicated GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the F80alds_v7 achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core execution, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and large-block memory bandwidth. Its integrated local NVMe storage and high raw processing power support exceptional Redis operations and static web serving throughput. Because memory capacity is limited to 2 GB per core, workloads requiring deep in-memory caching must be distributed horizontally. The server is well suited for high-concurrency batch processing, compression pipelines, large-scale CI/CD builds, and high-throughput key-value storage workloads demanding fast local I/O.
